title: Microservices Architecture
diagramContent:
graph TD
  Client --> API_Gateway[API Gateway (Express)]
  API_Gateway --> Auth[Auth Service (Express)]
  API_Gateway --> Billing[Billing Service (Express)]
  API_Gateway --> Inventory[Inventory Service (Express)]
  
  Auth --> DB1[(User DB)]
  Billing --> DB2[(Billing DB)]
  Inventory --> DB3[(Inventory DB)]
definition: Instead of building a massive monolithic Express app, you can build multiple smaller Express apps (microservices) that each handle a single domain (e.g., Auth Service, Billing Service, Product Service). They communicate with each other over HTTP or via Message Brokers.
simpleExplanation: Instead of building a massive monolithic Express app, you can build multiple smaller Express apps (microservices) that each handle a single domain (e.g., Auth Service, Billing Service, Product Service).

answers.question: Define Microservices Architecture in your own words.
answers.answer: Instead of building a massive monolithic Express app, you can build multiple smaller Express apps (microservices) that each handle a single domain (e.g., Auth Service, Billing Service, Product Service).

answers.question: When should you avoid using Microservices Architecture?
answers.answer: It depends on the specific architectural requirements and performance bottlenecks of your application. Overusing it can sometimes lead to tightly coupled code.
